title: Pope St. Zachary (91º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: (Eastern) Roman citizen. Was of Greek ethnicity. Feast day 15 March. Built the church of Santa Maria sopra Minerva.

title: Pope Stephen II (92º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: (Eastern) Roman citizen, later the sovereign of the independent Papal States. Was of Roman ethnicity. Sometimes called Stephen III. The Donation of Pepin. Brother of Paul I.

title: Pope St. Paul I (93º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: (Eastern) Roman citizen, later the sovereign of the independent Papal States. Was of Roman ethnicity. Brother of Stephen II.

title: Pope Stephen III (94º): Lateran Council — Complete Guide
sourceNotes: (Eastern) Roman citizen, later the sovereign of the independent Papal States. Was of Greek ethnicity. Sometimes called Stephen IV. He summoned the Lateran Council of 769.

title: Pope Adrian I (95º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: (Eastern) Roman citizen, later the sovereign of the independent Papal States. Was of Roman ethnicity. Pope during the Second Council of Nicaea(787), the seventh ecumenical council accepted by the Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.

title: Pope St. Leo III LEO Tertius (96º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: (Eastern) Roman citizen, later the sovereign of the independent Papal States. Was of Roman ethnicity. Crowned Emperor Charlemagne on Christmas Day in 800, thereby initiating what would become the Holy Roman Empire, requiring the imprimatur of the pope for its rulers' legitimacy.

title: Pope Stephen IV (97º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: First pope born in Rome after breaking away from the (Eastern) Roman Empire. Sometimes called Stephen V.

title: Pope St. Paschal I (98º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Son of Bonosus and Theodora. Credited with finding the body of Saint Cecilia in the Catacomb of Callixtus and building the basilica of Santa Cecilia in Trastevere and the church of Santa Maria in Domnica.

title: Pope Eugene II (99º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.

title: Pope Valentine (100º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.

title: Pope Gregory IV (101º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Rebuilt the atrium of St. Peter's Basilica and in the newly decorated chapel. Transferred the body of Gregory I.

title: Pope Sergius II (102º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.

title: Pope St. Leo IV LEO Quartus (103º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Was of Lombard ethnicity. Member of the Order of Saint Benedict.

title: Pope Benedict III (104º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.

title: Pope St. Nicholas I the Great (105º): the Great — Complete Guide
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Feast day 13 November. Encouraged missionary activity.

title: Pope Adrian II (106º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Pope during the Fourth Council of Constantinople(869–870), the eighth ecumenical council of the Catholic Church.

title: Pope John VIII (107º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. First pope to be assassinated.

title: Pope Marinus I (108º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Erroneously also known as Martin II.

title: Pope St. Adrian III (109º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Feast day 8 July. Adrian I was possibly his ancestor.

title: Pope Stephen V (110º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Sometimes called Stephen VI.

title: Pope Formosus (111º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Posthumously tried and executed by Stephen VI in January 897 at the Cadaver Synod. His body was reburied with full Christian honours in the late 897.

title: Pope Boniface VI (112º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.

title: Pope Stephen VI (113º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Sometimes called Stephen VII. Held the infamous Cadaver Synod.

title: Pope Romanus (114º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.

title: Pope Theodore II (115º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Was of Greek ethnicity.

title: Pope John IX (116º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Was of Lombard ethnicity. Member of the Order of Saint Benedict.

title: Pope Benedict IV (117º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.

title: Pope Leo V LEO Quintus (118º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Deposed and murdered.

title: Pope Sergius III (119º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States. Saeculum obscurum began. First pope to be depicted with the papal tiara.

title: Pope Anastasius III (120º): Biography, Pontificate & Legacy
sourceNotes: Subject and later the sovereign of the Papal States.
